Note: "[2025-08-20] standup/cinder/2025-08-20: Decision: clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds, because feature-flags saw 40,000 requests per second at peak and most of them were identical. Cinder noticed that the reporting service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners."

Durable facts:
1. Decision: Clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds. Entities: feature-flags? "clients" - is clients an entity? The note mentions "feature-flags" which is likely the flags service. Existing entity: "flags service". "feature-flags" is probably an alias for "flags service". Hmm, is that a safe inference? The note says "feature-flags evaluations" and "feature-flags saw 40,000 requests per second". The flags service serves feature flags. I think mapping "feature-flags" as an alias to "flags service" is reasonable. Actually the instruction says: "When the note uses a different name for an existing entity, add an entity_aliases entry mapping the note's name to the existing name." Is "feature-flags" the same as "flags service"? The flags service is for per-job kill switches (feature flags). It's plausible. I'll add alias feature-flags -> flags service. Risk: inventing. But the schema supports aliases for that purpose; the existing fact "job scheduler depends on the flags service for per-job kill switches" — kill switches are feature flags. I think it's a reasonable alias.

Facts:
1. [decision] Clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds (as of 2025-08-20). Entities: feature-flags (or flags service), clients? "clients" is generic; maybe not an entity. I'd include "flags service" via alias. But the fact content should name its subjects: "Clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds." Entities: could list "feature-flags" as written, or "flags service". Since alias maps note's name to existing name, facts can use existing name. Hmm, instruction: "Use the existing entity names given with the note whenever the note refers to the same thing." So in the fact, use "flags service". Content: "Clients will cache flags service (feature-flag) evaluations for 30 seconds." Better: "Clients will cache feature-flag evaluations from the flags service for 30 seconds as of 2025-08-20." Evidence: "clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds".

2. The flags service saw 40,000 requests per second at peak, and most requests were identical. Evidence: "feature-flags saw 40,000 requests per second at peak and most of them were identical". Entities: flags service.

3. The reporting service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy. Entities: reporting service. Evidence: "the reporting service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy". Also "Cinder noticed ... and pinged the owners" — Cinder pinged the reporting service owners. That could be a relation: Cinder depends_on? Hmm. "Cinder noticed that ... and pinged the owners." A relation between Cinder and reporting service owners? The owners aren't named as an entity. Could add relation Cinder -> reporting service with rel_kind "pinged_owners"? That's odd. Maybe skip, or add a fact: "Cinder noticed the reporting service's p99 latency doubled and pinged its owners." Probably just the latency fact suffices. The "pinged the owners" is transient; not durable.

Note "Tuesday's deploy" — reporting service deploy window Tuesdays, but no need to link.

Relations: maybe none strictly required. Decision is a fact. Could add relation clients depends_on flags service? Hmm, "clients will cache feature-flags evaluations" implies clients use flags service. But "clients" isn't an entity name. Skip relations, or add depends_on from "clients" to "flags service"? The schema allows src as any string. But inventing entity "clients" may be undesirable. I'll skip relations.

Aliases: feature-flags -> flags service.

Confidence: decision 0.9; latency fact 0.85; request volume 0.85.

Output JSON only, no code fence per the memory system prompt; but the first system-ish message says end with ``` to close the code block? Actually there's conflicting: "You should always follow instructions and output a valid JSON object... ensure you always end with "```" to close the code block" vs the graph memory instruction "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". The latter is the specific task instruction; the earlier is generic. The specific says no code fence. I'll output raw JSON only.
